query:
The group regularly does a shared meal before dark-sky sessions — Cecilia organises these and they seem like part of the tradition. Does this actually apply to all members? If not, who opts out and how does the chat show this?

Options:
A. Jerome
B. Tomás
C. Ruth
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t2 @2026-02-06T20:36:00) ok back to Feb 17th logistics, do we want to do the group meal first or go straight to site? I was thinking Thai takeaway at mine at 6:30 then car share to Blackmoor by 8? 🍜🌟
[2] (about=Jerome, episodic, t2 @2026-02-06T20:38:00) I will go straight to site. I need to be set up and aligned by 7:45 to make the most of the window. dinner beforehand doesn't work with my acquisition schedule.
[3] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t8 @2026-05-08T20:32:00) ok ok I hear you both, maybe we do need to do one proper dark-sky trip this summer. I'll organise it!!! Two-hour drive is doable if we make a weekend of it and get accommodation 🌟✨
[4] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t1 @2026-02-06T20:18:00) @all new moon is Feb 17th and the week around it looks really promising!!! I'm putting together a Cecilia's Big Nebula Night pitch 🌟 we deserve a proper session after January kept letting us down!!!
[5] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:35:00) everyone is in for September then!!! I'll send the formal group announcement Monday with three days notice, Nadia and Ruth as usual you want to co-sign the session note?!!! 🌟🌟🌟
[6] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:29:00) I came to a public star party three years ago expecting to be bored and left having already signed up for the next session. I think most people here have a version of that story. One look at something real through an eyepiece and that's it, you're done. I am organising the annual dark-sky weekend again for next October and I would love for Harriet to record the whole event for the podcast!!! 🌟🌟🌟
[7] (about=Harriet, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:38:00) Looking back at this year: Jerome on nebulae, Tomás on a proper mount, Ruth converted to dark sites, Cecilia blending Ha. Nadia and Ruth still the constants at the centre of it all. I think this group has had its best year yet and I am going to make sure the podcast reflects that. How would you each describe what this summer gave you that you did not have in January?
[8] (about=Harriet, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:26:00) This is exactly the episode I want to make. The group as a portrait. Nadia and Ruth as the founders, each of you arriving at a different moment for a different reason. Tomás because of the landscape photography crossover. Marcus because his kids gave him a telescope as a joke. Me because I came to write about it and could not leave. There is a book in this, not just an episode.
[9] (about=Ruth, episodic, t4 @2026-03-06T20:10:00) Is it possible that we compromise, perhaps one deeper-dark-sky session per season for those who want it, with Blackmoor remaining the default? That way nobody is left out on the regular outings.
[10] (about=Ruth, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:44:00) In favour. Though I would note that for a pure double-star session on a steady night, Blackmoor is still adequate. Seeing matters more than darkness for splitting tight pairs.
[11] (about=Ruth, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:37:00) I cannot speak to the technical aspects but the image looks beautiful. Is it possible that what you have both done this evening is exactly the kind of collaboration that makes this group worth belonging to?
[12] (about=Nadia, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:26:00) Ruth, that is perhaps the most gratifying thing I have heard in five years of this group. In my experience it takes one genuinely dark night to make the argument permanently. I am delighted the weekend did that for you.
[13] (about=Harriet, episodic, t8 @2026-05-08T20:40:00) I want to do an episode built around that weekend. The group, the dark sky, the contrast between people seeing it for the first time and veterans like Nadia who have been chasing this for thirty years. Dev, your reaction on the night would be perfect audio.

But I want to add something: this group started in Nadia's back garden, did it not? Nadia, Ruth, you two dragged everyone here. I think people forget that the whole thing was your idea originally.

Ruth, you said something on Saturday night that I think is going to be the opening line of the episode. About how you have been recommending books about dark skies for years but had never actually experienced one. Is it all right if I use that?
[16] (about=Ruth, episodic, t0 @2026-01-09T20:50:00) Nadia and I will sort the session reminder on Monday as usual. We will aim for 8pm arrive, first light by 8:30.
[17] (about=Harriet, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:20:00) I want to pick up the thread Harriet left last month about how this group started. Nadia, can I ask you properly: what was it like the first time you got people together in your back garden? You and Ruth, was it just the two of you at first?
[18] (about=Harriet, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:04:00) Harriet confirmed the marathon night and will put a reminder in the group; she asked Nadia and Ruth to send the formal session note Monday as usual, with three days notice minimum for the site.
[19] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:22:00) Ruth and I met at the county natural-history society in 2021 and discovered within about twenty minutes that we both preferred the stars to anything else on the programme. We agreed to meet the following Friday with our own telescopes in my back garden. There were two of us, a 4-inch refractor, Ruth's old 80mm, and a thermos of tea. I remember we stayed out until 2am on a school night and neither of us could see the point of going in. It grew from there one person at a time. In my experience the quiet beginning is the only honest beginning a group like this can have.
[20] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:04:00) Cecilia reprocessed her Orion Nebula and the Ha channel looks muddy compared to Jerome's images; she is genuinely asking for help with her DSLR workflow.
[21] (about=Cecilia, core, t8 @2026-05-08T20:16:00) Cecilia agreed to organise a proper dark-sky weekend trip this summer, suggesting a two-hour drive with accommodation.
[22] (about=Cecilia, core, t14 @2026-08-07T20:11:00) Cecilia came to a public star party three years ago expecting to be bored and left having signed up for the next session; she is organising the annual dark-sky weekend again for next October and wants Harriet to record the whole event for the podcast.
[23] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:38:00) dev and I stayed up till 3am watching jupiter and saturn transit. the seeing came up to 4/5 around 1am and at 400x on jupiter you could see three festoons in the NEB simultaneously. that's the best planetary night I've had in two years
[24] (about=Nadia, episodic, t8 @2026-05-08T20:31:00) I have been saying this since session one. In my experience there is no substitute for genuine darkness. The Milky Way shadow phenomenon happens around SQM 22.0 or above. You cannot replicate it closer to town, full stop.
[25] (about=Ruth, said_by=Harriet, profile, t10 @2026-06-05T20:23:00) Harriet noted Ruth said on Saturday night that she had been recommending books about dark skies for years but had never actually experienced one; Harriet wants to use it as the episode's opening line.
[26] (about=Ruth, core, t4 @2026-03-06T19:49:00) Ruth proposes a compromise of one deeper-dark-sky session per season for those who want it, with Blackmoor remaining the default.
agent_answer:
**A. Jerome**

Cecilia proposed the pre-session group meal — Thai takeaway at hers at 6:30 before car-sharing to Blackmoor. Jerome opted out, saying he would **go straight to site** because he needed to be set up and aligned by 7:45, and that **“dinner beforehand doesn't work with my acquisition schedule.”** So the shared meal does **not** apply to all members; the chat shows Jerome skipping it for his setup schedule.
